messages:
maya: Heads up — the python async streaming example in the onboarding sample is broken for me. The code in docs uses `async for chunk in client.stream()` but my client returns a sync iterator and the Sphinx page linked from the README 404s :confused:

kevin: oh no. which repo/sample? can you paste the exact snippet and the SDK version? :eyes:

maya: sample-app/examples/streaming_async.py (cloned today). SDK pinned to 0.11.0 in requirements.txt. stack trace is just TypeError: 'generator' object is not async-iterable when i run `python -m examples.streaming_async`

maya: snippet:

```python
# streaming_async.py (excerpt)
async def main():
    client = RedwoodClient.from_env()
    async for chunk in client.stream("gpt-small", "tell me a joke"):
        print(chunk)
```

kevin: that signature changed in 0.12.0 — we switched to returning an async generator only when you call `.astream()` to avoid breaking sync callers. looks like the docs weren't updated. also the Sphinx link in the README points to /docs/streaming which got moved to /guides/streaming.

sam: i ran the link checker on the site yesterday, it flagged that page but the PR to fix it got stuck in reviews. i'll dig it up.

doc-bot: Automated Link Check: FOUND 1 broken link in /sample-app/README.md -> https://docs.redwood.ai/docs/streaming (404)

eli: quick workaround: change code to `async for chunk in client.astream("gpt-small", "..."):` or pin sdk==0.11.* if you need the old behavior. i'm about to open a tiny docs PR to update example and README.

maya: thanks eli — switching to `astream` fixed my run. can we also add a typing note? mypy complains because the stub says `Iterator[str]` not `AsyncIterator[str]`

kevin: good catch. typing drift is real. i'll add a follow-up task to update the stub types for streaming returns and add a tiny test to CI to catch mismatch. filing an issue now.

sam: PR for README link -> #4623. PR for example change -> #4624. tagging @devex for QA before merge.

maya: perfect — appreciate the quick turnaround. leaving this thread for anyone hitting the same error. :thumbsup:
